title: Beans (Common Bean) — East Africa Farming Guide
content:
## Common Beans (Phaseolus vulgaris)

Beans are the most important legume crop for food security and nutrition in East Africa. Often intercropped with maize.

### Varieties

**Bush beans (determinate, 60–80 days):**
- Rose Coco (Rosecoco) — most popular in Kenya; large red-speckled grain; good market price
- Lyamungu 85 — Tanzania; good yields; bean fly resistant
- K132 — Kenya; small red bean; fast maturing

**Climbing beans (80–100 days):**
- Selian 97 — Tanzania highlands; very high yields on trellises
- HM21–7 — Kenya; popular in western highlands

### Planting

- **Season:** Plant at onset of rains
- **Spacing:** 40–50cm rows × 15–20cm plants; 2 seeds per hole
- **Seed rate:** 60–80 kg/ha (bush) or 40–60 kg/ha (climbing)
- **Depth:** 3–5cm

### Fertilizer

- Beans fix nitrogen — do NOT apply heavy nitrogen fertilizer
- Apply phosphorus at planting: DAP 30 kg/ha or TSP 25 kg/ha
- Rhizobium inoculant on seed before planting boosts yields 20–30% on soils lacking natural rhizobia
- Foliar micronutrients (Boron, Zinc) at flowering improve pod set

### Bean Fly (Ophiomyia spp.)

Most damaging pest of beans in East Africa, especially at seedling stage.

**Symptoms:** Wilting and death of seedlings; yellow swelling at stem base; maggots visible inside stem.

**Control:**
- Seed treatment with Imidacloprid (Gaucho, Confidor) before planting
- Thiamethoxam (Cruiser) seed dressing
- Spray Dimethoate or Malathion at first sign (V1–V2 stage)
- Cultural: plant at optimal density; avoid planting in bean-fly-endemic areas during peak season

## Maharagwe (Phaseolus vulgaris)

Maharagwe ni zao muhimu la protini na usalama wa chakula Afrika Mashariki. Mara nyingi hupandwa pamoja na mahindi.

### Mbolea

Maharagwe yanafuga nitrojeni — USITUMIE mbolea nyingi ya nitrojeni.
Weka fosforasi wakati wa upanzi: DAP kilo 30/hekta.

title: Cassava — Drought-Tolerant Staple for Africa
content:
## Cassava (Manihot esculenta)

Cassava is the third most important food crop in Sub-Saharan Africa. It is extremely drought-tolerant and grows on poor soils where other crops fail.

### Varieties

**East Africa improved varieties:**
- **Nase 14** — Uganda; CMD-resistant; high starch; 10–14 months maturity
- **Tajirika** — Tanzania; CMD and CBSD resistant; widely promoted
- **KME1** — Kenya coast; CMD tolerant

**Warning:** Do NOT plant local varieties in areas with Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD) or Cassava Brown Streak Disease (CBSD) — use certified improved varieties only.

### Planting

- Propagate from stem cuttings (20–30cm long, 3–5 nodes)
- Plant cuttings at 30–45° angle, 2/3 in the ground
- Spacing: 1m × 1m for food (10,000 plants/ha) or 1m × 0.8m for high density
- Best time: beginning of rains
- Do NOT plant in waterlogged soil — cassava rots easily

### Key Pests and Diseases

1. **Cassava Mosaic Disease (CMD)** — caused by whitefly-transmitted virus; use resistant varieties
2. **Cassava Brown Streak Disease (CBSD)** — tuber necrosis; use resistant varieties
3. **Cassava Mealybug** — stunts plants; spray with Karate or use parasitic wasp biocontrol
4. **Green Spider Mite** — dry season pest; spray acaricide or use neem extract

### Harvesting

- Harvest at 8–24 months depending on variety and purpose
- Fresh roots: harvest at 8–10 months for best eating quality
- Starch/flour: harvest at 12–18 months for higher starch content
- Dry roots immediately after harvest (cassava deteriorates within 48 hours of harvest)
